A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReFusion research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark performance and throughput, controlled retraining, token-dependency measurements, ablations, scaling experiments, and generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds certainty-scoring comparisons and generated-length/latency results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The default slot selection, verification and infilling procedure, token reordering, KV-cache concatenation, and hybrid training objectives remain unchanged. Renaming planning to selection and explicitly explaining remasking of unaccepted drafts clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The training datasets in Appendix B.1 and the seven evaluation benchmarks remain the same. The new analyses reuse this coverage; the 120K controlled-training subset and scaling to 14M samples already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: New Appendix C.2/Table 7 evaluates mean slot probability and mean slot entropy against the default first-token probability rule, adding two component-level comparison methods. External comparator membership in the main, controlled, and broader model comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.6/Table 9 adds average generated length and measured inference latency in seconds to the evaluation measures. Existing zero-shot evaluation, A100 batch-size-one throughput measurement, and the 120K-sample, ten-epoch controlled comparison remain as reported. Changed Table 2 scores do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a certainty-scoring ablation and a length/latency analysis examining whether quality gains arise from longer outputs. The KV-cache ablation is retained, moving from v1 Section 5.5/Table 4 to v2 Appendix C.3/Table 8. Existing dependency, hyperparameter, scaling, and case analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises baseline results under the same stated protocol: retrained LLaDA's average task score changes from 14.43 to 47.41 and average TPS from 0.41 to 4.24. Retrained Qwen3-8B's HumanEval score changes from 53.66 to 63.72, narrowing ReFusion's unchanged 70.12 score advantage from 16.46 to 6.40 points. Tables 7 and 9 add scoring and length/latency results; Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds the explicit RoPE attention identity and positional-invariance argument in Equation 1, plus an algebraic explanation connecting masked-token normalization to implicit 1/t weighting. The training losses, inference equations, and Appendix A.1 combinatorial analysis otherwise remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about full KV-cache reuse, flexible slot generation, reduced learning complexity, and performance/efficiency advantages. The headline 34% performance gain, over 18-fold MDM speedup, and 2.33-fold ARM speedup are unchanged; emphasizing sequence reorganization reframes the existing contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.2 explains first-token confidence as an anchor for infilling and interprets scoring agreement as robustness. Appendix C.6 argues that shorter outputs and lower latency support methodological efficiency, but its new MMLU-Pro superiority assertion contradicts Table 1. The immutable-slot limitation and KV-cache regularization explanation are retained.

D1.justification: Sections 4.2 and A.3 newly specify that unverified or partially verified draft slots are remasked before the next selection cycle, clarifying implementation of the existing shortcut. Appendix B's hyperparameters, hardware, training cost, and EOS handling remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement reiterates existing code access rather than establishing newly available resources.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 2 expands positioning relative to block-based diffusion through explicit discussion of motivation, decoding direction, caching, and hierarchical compatibility, including positioning ReFusion as a more general framework.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the methodological narrative around sequence reorganization, rewrites the abstract and introductory framing, and consistently replaces planning terminology with selection. It moves the dependency pilot and KV-cache ablation into appendices and adds acknowledgments, a reproducibility statement, and an LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a token-reordering diagram and two result tables, revises the overview and detailed inference annotations, and relocates the dependency plot and KV-cache table. Existing empirical plots and the overall visual style are retained; numerical revisions to Table 2 do not constitute a table redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves methodological clarity and adds useful scoring and latency evidence. However, it does not explain the substantial controlled-baseline revisions in Table 2, and new Appendix C.6 claims superior MMLU-Pro performance over Qwen3-8B despite Table 1 reporting 45.94 versus 67.25. These evidential and interpretive concerns coexist with the clearer exposition and added analyses, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
